chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Musa ibn al-Hasan, from al-Sayyari, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from the one who informed him, from Ismail ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimi, who said:
I complained to Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about the rumbling that afflicted me in my stomach and the scarcity of my digestion of food.

So he said to me: 'Why do you not take Nabidh which we drink, and it digests the food and removes the rumbling and the winds from the belly?' I said to him: 'Describe it for me, may I be sacrificed for you.'

So he said to me: 'Take a Sa' of raisins, so clean its seeds and whatever is in it, then wash it with water with a good washing. Then soak it in an equal amount of water or whatever submerges it. Then leave it in the winter for three days and nights, and in the summer for one day and one night. So when that time is up, you strain it and take its clear liquid and put it in a vessel, and take its measure with a stick. Then cook it gently until two-thirds of it goes away and one-third remains.'
Then put half a ratl of honey on it, and take the measure of the honey. Then cook it until that increment evaporates.
Then take ginger, Alpinia, cinnamon, saffron, cloves, and mastic resin, and pound them and put them in a thin cloth, and drop it in and boil it with it with a boil. Then take it off.
So when it has cooled, strain it and take from it for your lunch and your dinner.
He said: 'So I did it, and it removed from me what I was feeling, and it was a pleasant drink. It does not change if it remains, God willing.'

key_terms.خُولِنْجَان: Alpinia galanga, a type of ginger relative
key_terms.رِطْل: A traditional unit of weight measurement
key_terms.صَاع: A traditional unit of volume measurement
key_terms.قَرَاقِر: Rumbling or gurgling sounds in the stomach
key_terms.نَبِيذ: A traditional fermented drink made from raisins or dates

ai.seo_question: What is the recipe for Nabidh to aid digestion according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Kafi* highlights the Prophetic tradition of using Nabidh not merely as a beverage but as a therapeutic remedy for digestive ailments, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the integration of spiritual and physical well-being. The detailed prescription by Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) underscores the scientific precision in traditional Islamic medicine, where specific ingredients like ginger and mastic are utilized for their carminative and soothing properties. It serves as a practical guide for believers to maintain health through natural, Sunnah-based remedies.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Musa Bin Al Hassan, from Al Sayyari, from Muhammad Bin Al Husayn, from the one who informed him, from Ismail Bin Al Fazl Al Hashimy who said, 
‘I complained to Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> of the rumbling and the winds in my stomach, and the scarcity of my digestion of the food’.

So heasws said to me: ‘Why do you not take Nabeez which weasws drink and it digests the food and removes the rumbling and the winds from the belly?’ So I said to himasws, ‘Describe it for me, may I be sacrificed for youasws’.

So heasws said to me: ‘Take a Sa’a (a unit of measurement - four handfuls) of raisins, so clean its seeds and whatever is in it, then wash it with water with a renewed washing. Then soak it in similar from the water or whatever submerges it. Then leave it in the winter for three days and nights, and in the summer, for one day and one night. So when that times comes up so you take it and make it to be in a vessel, and take its measurement with a stick. Then cook it gently until two-thirds of it goes away and there remains one-third of it.
Then make half a ratl (unit of measurement) of honey to be upon it, and take a measurement of the honey. Then cook it until that increment evaporates.

Then take ginger and Alpinia (a plant), and cinnamon, and the saffron, and cloves, and mastic resin, and pound these and make these to be in a thin rag, and place it in is and boil it with it with a boiling.
Then take it off. So when it has cooled, clean it and take from it upon your lunch and your dinner’.
He (the narrator) said, ‘So I did it, and it removed from me what I had, and it was an aromatic drink. It will not change, when it remains (for a while), Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Willing’.
en.sarwar: 3. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Musa ibn al-Hassan from al-Sayyariy from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn from those who narrated to him from ’Isma‘il ibn al-Fadl al-Hashimy who has said the following:
“I once complained before abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about growling in my stomach and my not being able to digest food.

He (the Imam) said, ‘Why do you not drink al-Nabidh which we drink? It digests food and takes away abdominal growling and gases.’ I then asked, ‘Please describe it for me, I pray to Allah to keep my soul in service for your cause.’

He (the Imam) said, ‘Take one Sa‘ of raisins, clean it of seeds and other things in it, then wash it properly, then soak it with an equal amount of water or a quantity that covers it. In winter leave it for three days and nights, and in summer one day and night. Thereafter clean it and take the cleaned amount, place it in a pot and take its measurement with a piece of wood then cook it gently until its two-thirds are gone and one-third is left.
Then place in it one-half ritl of honey. Take this honey and cook it until the extra is gone

then take ginger, Khulinjana (a certain Indian plant) and cinnamon, saffron, dianthus and Mustakiy (Mastic tree) powder them and place them in a piece of fine cloth. Place it in to cook and boil it with the rest, then take it away from the fire.
When it is cool clean it. You can take from it after your lunch and dinner.’
He (the narrator) has said, ‘I followed the instruction and my condition that I had was gone. It is a fine drink and does not change if it remains for a time, by the will of Allah.’”
